correctness.rationale: Exact Q facets are the Cartesian product of a coordinate simplex and a free cube; determinant k gives sqrt(k)/(k-1)! area. Weight ratios are explicit and strictly decreasing; a controlled local log-ratio expansion and geometric Gaussian tail domination yield a normalized N(0,1/2) local limit. The b-weight ratio proves S/V ~ d^(3/4). Complete finite convex-hull checks in d=2..5 independently reproduce shell areas and volume. Experiments are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The body is a canonical polytope whose face count and polar angular law are established. A complete Euclidean facet-area metric invariant reveals concentration on normals of square-root support although the count-typical facet has linear support, with a sharp local Gaussian limit, asymptotically surface-area-dominating subexponential facet set and S/V ~ d^(3/4). This is structural geometry, not a small computational increment.
